subject: Re: competitive review — request to match incumbent + migration support
messages:
From: Megan O'Connor <megan@orchard.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@orchard.ai
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Competitive review — can Redwood match incumbent package?

Hi Dylan,

Quick one — we're re-evaluating our inference stack and the incumbent vendor (BigLambda) has come back with a renewal that includes a 20% list discount + six months of free inference credits if we sign by end of May. Before we proceed to procurement, we wanted to check whether Redwood can match or beat that package and what migration assistance you'd offer.

What matters most to us:
- Effective per-token/unit economics over 12 months (not just list discount)
- Credits or free dedicated capacity to cover initial migration load
- Any migration engineering support / onboarding runway

I can share a usage snapshot; attached is a brief summary of current consumption (Q1). Can we get a quick counteroffer and an indicative timeline?

Thanks,
Megan
Megan O'Connor
Head of Platform Ops
Orchard.ai

Attachment: usage_snapshot_q1.csv
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Megan O'Connor <megan@orchard.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 18:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Competitive review — can Redwood match incumbent package?

Hi Megan — really appreciate you reaching out and sharing the current snapshot. Short answer: we can be competitive, but the final shape depends on exact usage mix, peak concurrency, and retention/latency SLOs.

Next steps I propose:
1) You send the last 90 days of token/embedding counts and peak concurrency windows (CSV is great).
2) We run a quick cost model and a migration estimate.
3) We return a written counter with: an economic comparison (12-month TCO), a migration credit proposal, and a proposed ramp plan.

I'm attaching a one-page usage template to make step (1) quick. If you can get that back by EOD tomorrow, we can aim to deliver a formal counter within 48 hours.

High-level options I can already tee up:
- Price match (list discount-style) + 3 months of dedicated credits; or
- Slightly smaller discount + extended migration engineering hours and playbook.

Which matters more: deeper up-front credits or lower long-term unit price? That will help me nail the counter.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive — Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
Attachment: usage_template.xlsx
From: Megan O'Connor <megan@orchard.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Competitive review — can Redwood match incumbent package?

Thanks Dylan — attaching the snapshot you asked for. A few clarifications:
- Our Q1 consumption is bursty: 70% baseline, 30% short peaks (20–30 min) during batch scoring windows.
- Target latency: P95 < 450ms for critical user flows.
- Incumbent offer details (summary): 20% off list for 12 months + 6 months free inference credits equating to ~$120k. No committed migration SLA but they offered 40 hours of onboarding support.

We'd prefer deeper up-front credits to offset migration cost, but long-term unit economics are important too. Also, we need a clear fallback plan: if quality regresses or latency issues arise during ramp, procurement wants a short escape clause with credits.

Appended: usage_snapshot_q1.csv

Megan
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Competitive review — Orchard wants a match; need a recommended counter and migration terms

Forwarding Orchard's snapshot and incumbent summary. Key asks from Procurement: price match + migration credits; they also want an escape clause if latency/quality dips. Can you propose a defensible counter we can send by EOD?

Some ideas to consider:
- 18% list discount for 12 months + $80k dedicated + 2 months free dedicated capacity credits (covers 75% of estimated migration spend)
- Include a 60-day quality SLA clause: if performance regresses beyond agreed thresholds, we provide additional credits and a prioritized incident runbook.
- Optional: startup-style ramp credits if they commit to a 12-month minimum usage baseline.

Please reply with redlines and an attached term sheet.

Thanks,
Dylan

-----Original message attached-----
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Competitive review — Orchard wants a match; need a recommended counter and migration terms

Quick proposed counter (for external):
- 18% off list across core inference and embedding units for 12 months
- $90,000 migration credit applied as dedicated capacity credits (usable during first 90 days of contract)
- Migration engineering: up to 80 hours of SRE/solutions support at no charge (kickoff + 30-day ramp + 60-day stabilization)
- SLA & escape: 60-day trial window from first go-live; if Orchard documents verified degradation against agreed eval prompts (quality or latency), we provide an additional $30k credit and a 30-day remediation commitment.

Rationale: beaches the incumbent's 20% discount with a stronger migration package and a pragmatic SLA that reduces procurement risk without hammering margin. We preserve the ability to revisit unit pricing at Q4 with usage thresholds.

Attached: redwood_price_match_term_sheet_v1.pdf, migration_plan_slide_deck.pptx

-Neha
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Megan O'Connor <megan@orchard.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Competitive review — can Redwood match incumbent package?

Hi Megan — thanks for the snapshot and the clarity on what's most important. After internal review here is our formal counter-proposal:

Offer summary (12-month term):
- Unit economics: 18% off published list rates for inference and embeddings for 12 months
- Migration credit: $90,000 in dedicated capacity credits (applied within first 90 days)
- Migration support: up to 80 hours of dedicated engineering (SRE + Solutions) to run cutover, performance tuning, and a ramp stabilization plan
- Trial / escape protections: a 60-day observable window from go-live. If Orchard documents regression on agreed eval prompts (either quality or latency beyond agreed thresholds), we will issue an additional $30k credit and commit to a 30-day prioritized remediation plan.

Why this is competitive: it approximates the incumbent's economic uplift while materially lowering Orchard's migration risk through a larger credit + SRE hours. We can also commit to a 2-week dedicated runbook handoff and a tech-walkthrough for your engineering leads.

If that package sounds reasonable, I'll follow with a short term sheet and a proposed kickoff plan (dates and owners). Would you prefer a DocuSign or an initial pilot amendment to your current PO?

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive — Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0132
Attachment: redwood_price_match_term_sheet_v1.pdf
